```{r}
# R/02_load_all.R
# Goal: Combine all 40 participant .RData files into one tidy tibble.

library(tidyverse)
library(here)

# === Step 1: List the files ===
rdata_files <- list.files(here("Rdata"), 
                          pattern = "_final\\.RData$", 
                          full.names = TRUE)

cat("Found", length(rdata_files), "participant files\n")
# Should print 40 (or however many you have)

load_one_participant <- function(file_path) {
  # Extract participant ID from filename
  pid <- str_extract(basename(file_path), "[Pp]\\d+")
  
  # Load into a fresh environment
  env <- new.env()
  load(file_path, envir = env)
  
  # Pull out the data frame
  df <- env$data
  
  # === FIX: handle unnamed / NA-named columns ===
  current_names <- names(df)
  
  # Identify problem columns
  bad <- is.na(current_names) | current_names == ""
  
  if (any(bad)) {
    # Give them placeholder names (we'll drop them right after)
    current_names[bad] <- paste0("unnamed_", seq_len(sum(bad)))
    names(df) <- current_names
    
    # Drop the unnamed columns — they're analysis artifacts, not real data
    df <- df[, !startsWith(names(df), "unnamed_"), drop = FALSE]
  }
  
  # === Now the rest of the processing ===
  df$ID <- pid
  df <- df %>% filter(!is.na(finish))
  
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      start_time = as.POSIXct(start, format = "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M"),
      hrs_from_start = as.numeric(
        difftime(start_time, min(start_time, na.rm = TRUE), units = "hours")
      )
    )
  
  df <- df %>%
    arrange(start_time) %>%
    mutate(gap_hrs = c(NA, diff(hrs_from_start)))
  
  df <- df %>%
    select(ID, start_time, hrs_from_start, gap_hrs, everything())
  
  df
}
# === Step 3: Load all participants ===
fisher_all <- map_dfr(rdata_files, load_one_participant)

# === Step 4: Sanity checks ===
cat("\n--- Sanity Checks ---\n")
cat("Total rows (completed beeps across all participants):", nrow(fisher_all), "\n")
cat("Number of unique participants:", n_distinct(fisher_all$ID), "\n\n")

# Per-participant summary
participant_summary <- fisher_all %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  summarise(
    n_beeps = n(),
    duration_days = (max(hrs_from_start) - min(hrs_from_start)) / 24,
    median_gap_hrs = median(gap_hrs, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_gap_hrs = max(gap_hrs, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(participant_summary, n = 50)

# === Step 5: Save the combined dataset ===
# Create output dir if it doesn't exist
dir.create(here("data", "processed"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

saveRDS(fisher_all, here("data", "processed", "fisher_all.rds"))
saveRDS(participant_summary, here("data", "processed", "participant_summary.rds"))

cat("\nSaved to: data/processed/fisher_all.rds\n")
```

```{r}
# R/05_extract_groups.R (fixed)

library(tidyverse)
library(here)

rdata_files <- list.files(here("Rdata"), 
                          pattern = "_final\\.RData$", 
                          full.names = TRUE)

inspect_one <- function(file_path) {
  pid <- str_extract(basename(file_path), "[Pp]\\d+")
  env <- new.env()
  load(file_path, envir = env)
  
  # Just record what objects exist and their lengths
  obj_summary <- ls(env)
  
  # Try to find any objects that could be diagnostic labels
  # (single string/integer, or short labeled vector)
  candidates <- character(0)
  for (obj in obj_summary) {
    val <- env[[obj]]
    if (length(val) == 1 && (is.character(val) || is.factor(val))) {
      candidates <- c(candidates, paste0(obj, "=", val))
    }
  }
  
  tibble(
    ID = pid,
    n_objects = length(obj_summary),
    candidate_labels = paste(candidates, collapse = "; ")
  )
}

groups_df <- map_dfr(rdata_files, inspect_one)
print(groups_df, n = 40)

# Confirmation: no per-participant diagnostic label embedded in files
cat("\nConfirmed: no diagnostic group labels in the .RData files.\n")
cat("We'll get them from Fisher et al. 2017 Table 1 instead.\n")
```

```{r}
# R/06_per_person_smooths.R

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(mgcv)

# === Load data ===
fisher_all <- readRDS(here("data", "processed", "fisher_all.rds"))

if (!"session" %in% colnames(fisher_all)) {
  fisher_all <- fisher_all %>%
    group_by(ID) %>%
    arrange(start_time) %>%
    mutate(session = cumsum(replace_na(gap_hrs > 72, FALSE)) + 1) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# === Pick target item ===
target_item <- "down"

# === Build lag-augmented dataset ===
# Each row: (current value, lagged value, lag distance, person)

make_lag_data <- function(df, item, max_lag = 14) {
  df <- df %>% 
    filter(session == 1) %>%
    drop_na(all_of(item)) %>%
    group_by(ID) %>%
    arrange(start_time) %>%
    mutate(
      y_z = as.numeric(scale(.data[[item]])),
      beep_num = row_number()
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  expand_lags <- function(person_df) {
    map_dfr(1:max_lag, function(k) {
      person_df %>%
        mutate(
          y_lagged = lag(y_z, k),
          lag_value = k
        ) %>%
        select(ID, beep_num, lag_value, y_now = y_z, y_lagged)
    })
  }
  
  df %>%
    group_split(ID) %>%
    map_dfr(expand_lags) %>%
    drop_na()
}

cat("Building lag-augmented dataset for:", target_item, "\n")
lag_data <- make_lag_data(fisher_all, target_item)
cat("Total rows:", nrow(lag_data), "\n")
cat("Participants:", n_distinct(lag_data$ID), "\n")

lag_data$ID <- as.factor(lag_data$ID)

# === Factor-smooth GAMM ===
# Model: y_now = (population smooth over lag) + (person-specific smooth over lag)
#        all multiplied by y_lagged so it's a lag-effect curve
#
# This is the core of DTVEM-RE Stage 1 — each person gets their own smooth curve
# with shrinkage toward the population mean.

cat("\nFitting factor-smooth GAMM... (a few minutes)\n")

fs_gamm <- bam(
  y_now ~ s(lag_value, k = 8, by = y_lagged) +
          s(lag_value, ID, bs = "fs", k = 8, by = y_lagged),
  data = lag_data,
  discrete = TRUE,
  method = "fREML"
)

cat("\nDone fitting.\n")
cat("Model summary:\n")
print(summary(fs_gamm))

# === Build predictions for plotting ===
# Predict y_now / y_lagged at every lag for every person
# This gives the "effect of lagged value on current value at each lag"

pred_grid <- expand_grid(
  ID = unique(lag_data$ID),
  lag_value = seq(1, 14, by = 0.25)
) %>%
  mutate(y_lagged = 1)  # standardized

pred_grid$fitted <- predict(fs_gamm, newdata = pred_grid)

# === Plot 1: spaghetti plot — all 40 person-specific curves ===
dir.create(here("output", "person_smooths"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

p1 <- ggplot(pred_grid, aes(x = lag_value, y = fitted)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = ID), alpha = 0.25, color = "steelblue") +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line",
               aes(group = 1), color = "red", linewidth = 1.4) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Person-specific lag-effect curves: ", target_item, " predicting itself"),
    subtitle = paste0("Each blue line = one participant. Red line = population average. N = ",
                      n_distinct(lag_data$ID)),
    x = "Lag (beeps)",
    y = "Predicted effect on current value (z-scaled)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

print(p1)
ggsave(here("output", "person_smooths", paste0(target_item, "_AR_spaghetti.png")),
       p1, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 150)

# === Plot 2: heatmap — sort participants by their lag-1 effect ===
person_lag1 <- pred_grid %>%
  filter(abs(lag_value - 1) < 0.1) %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  summarise(lag1_effect = mean(fitted), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(lag1_effect)

pred_grid_sorted <- pred_grid %>%
  mutate(ID = factor(ID, levels = person_lag1$ID))

p2 <- ggplot(pred_grid_sorted, aes(x = lag_value, y = ID, fill = fitted)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0,
                       name = "Effect") +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Person-specific lag-effect curves: ", target_item, " AR"),
    subtitle = "Participants sorted by lag-1 effect magnitude",
    x = "Lag (beeps)",
    y = "Participant"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7))

print(p2)
ggsave(here("output", "person_smooths", paste0(target_item, "_AR_heatmap.png")),
       p2, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 150)

# === Numerical summary: variation in lag-1 effect across people ===
cat("\n=== Variation in lag-1 effect across participants ===\n")
cat("Mean lag-1 effect:", round(mean(person_lag1$lag1_effect), 3), "\n")
cat("SD lag-1 effect:", round(sd(person_lag1$lag1_effect), 3), "\n")
cat("Min lag-1 effect:", round(min(person_lag1$lag1_effect), 3), "\n")
cat("Max lag-1 effect:", round(max(person_lag1$lag1_effect), 3), "\n")

cat("\nLook at the spaghetti plot:\n")
cat("- If blue lines spread widely from the red → real person-specific variation → DTVEM-RE has a target\n")
cat("- If blue lines collapse onto red → no person-specific variation → reconsider\n")
```

```{r}
# R/07_per_person_replication.R
# Goal: Replicate the per-person heterogeneity finding from `down` on
# `worried` (anxiety) and `energetic` (positive affect).
# If the same pattern shows up, DTVEM-RE has robust empirical motivation.

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(mgcv)

# === Load data ===
fisher_all <- readRDS(here("data", "processed", "fisher_all.rds"))

if (!"session" %in% colnames(fisher_all)) {
  fisher_all <- fisher_all %>%
    group_by(ID) %>%
    arrange(start_time) %>%
    mutate(session = cumsum(replace_na(gap_hrs > 72, FALSE)) + 1) %>%
    ungroup()
}

dir.create(here("output", "person_smooths"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# === Reusable lag-data builder ===
make_lag_data <- function(df, item, max_lag = 14) {
  df <- df %>% 
    filter(session == 1) %>%
    drop_na(all_of(item)) %>%
    group_by(ID) %>%
    arrange(start_time) %>%
    mutate(
      y_z = as.numeric(scale(.data[[item]])),
      beep_num = row_number()
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  expand_lags <- function(person_df) {
    map_dfr(1:max_lag, function(k) {
      person_df %>%
        mutate(
          y_lagged = lag(y_z, k),
          lag_value = k
        ) %>%
        select(ID, beep_num, lag_value, y_now = y_z, y_lagged)
    })
  }
  
  df %>%
    group_split(ID) %>%
    map_dfr(expand_lags) %>%
    drop_na()
}

# === Function to fit GAMM and make plots for one item ===
fit_and_plot <- function(item) {
  cat("\n\n=================================\n")
  cat("ITEM:", item, "\n")
  cat("=================================\n")
  
  lag_data <- make_lag_data(fisher_all, item)
  cat("Rows:", nrow(lag_data), 
      "| Participants:", n_distinct(lag_data$ID), "\n")
  lag_data$ID <- as.factor(lag_data$ID)
  
  cat("Fitting factor-smooth GAMM...\n")
  fs_gamm <- bam(
    y_now ~ s(lag_value, k = 8, by = y_lagged) +
            s(lag_value, ID, bs = "fs", k = 8, by = y_lagged),
    data = lag_data,
    discrete = TRUE,
    method = "fREML"
  )
  
  # Prediction grid
  pred_grid <- expand_grid(
    ID = unique(lag_data$ID),
    lag_value = seq(1, 14, by = 0.25)
  ) %>%
    mutate(y_lagged = 1)
  
  pred_grid$fitted <- predict(fs_gamm, newdata = pred_grid)
  
  # Spaghetti plot
  p1 <- ggplot(pred_grid, aes(x = lag_value, y = fitted)) +
    geom_line(aes(group = ID), alpha = 0.25, color = "steelblue") +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line",
                 aes(group = 1), color = "red", linewidth = 1.4) +
    labs(
      title = paste0("Person-specific lag-effect curves: ", item, " AR"),
      subtitle = paste0("N = ", n_distinct(lag_data$ID)),
      x = "Lag (beeps)",
      y = "Predicted effect (z-scaled)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
  
  ggsave(here("output", "person_smooths", paste0(item, "_AR_spaghetti.png")),
         p1, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 150)
  
  # Heatmap
  person_lag1 <- pred_grid %>%
    filter(abs(lag_value - 1) < 0.1) %>%
    group_by(ID) %>%
    summarise(lag1_effect = mean(fitted), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(lag1_effect)
  
  pred_grid_sorted <- pred_grid %>%
    mutate(ID = factor(ID, levels = person_lag1$ID))
  
  p2 <- ggplot(pred_grid_sorted, aes(x = lag_value, y = ID, fill = fitted)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0,
                         name = "Effect") +
    labs(
      title = paste0("Person-specific lag-effect curves: ", item, " AR"),
      subtitle = "Sorted by lag-1 effect magnitude",
      x = "Lag (beeps)",
      y = "Participant"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7))
  
  ggsave(here("output", "person_smooths", paste0(item, "_AR_heatmap.png")),
         p2, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 150)
  
  # Numerical summary
  summary_stats <- tibble(
    item = item,
    n_persons = n_distinct(lag_data$ID),
    mean_lag1 = mean(person_lag1$lag1_effect),
    sd_lag1 = sd(person_lag1$lag1_effect),
    min_lag1 = min(person_lag1$lag1_effect),
    max_lag1 = max(person_lag1$lag1_effect),
    range_lag1 = max_lag1 - min_lag1
  )
  
  cat("\nLag-1 effect summary for", item, ":\n")
  print(summary_stats)
  
  # Show the two plots
  print(p1)
  
  list(stats = summary_stats, person_lag1 = person_lag1, pred_grid = pred_grid)
}

# === Run for worried and energetic ===
res_worried   <- fit_and_plot("worried")
res_energetic <- fit_and_plot("energetic")

# === Combined comparison ===
# Pull in the `down` results from before by re-fitting (so all three are comparable)
res_down <- fit_and_plot("down")

# Stack the lag-1 distributions
all_lag1 <- bind_rows(
  res_down$person_lag1   %>% mutate(item = "down"),
  res_worried$person_lag1 %>% mutate(item = "worried"),
  res_energetic$person_lag1 %>% mutate(item = "energetic")
)

# Boxplot/jitter: distribution of person-specific lag-1 effects across items
p_comparison <- ggplot(all_lag1, aes(x = item, y = lag1_effect)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.5, alpha = 0.4, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.6, size = 1.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Person-specific lag-1 AR effects across items",
    subtitle = "Each dot = one participant. Spread shows between-person heterogeneity.",
    x = "EMA item",
    y = "Lag-1 autoregressive effect"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

print(p_comparison)
ggsave(here("output", "person_smooths", "comparison_lag1_distributions.png"),
       p_comparison, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 150)

# === Combined summary table ===
combined <- bind_rows(res_down$stats, res_worried$stats, res_energetic$stats)
cat("\n\n=== COMBINED SUMMARY ===\n")
print(combined)

# Save everything
saveRDS(list(down = res_down, worried = res_worried, energetic = res_energetic),
        here("output", "person_smooths", "per_person_results.rds"))

cat("\nDone. Three pairs of plots saved to output/person_smooths/.\n")
cat("Key question: does the spread for `worried` and `energetic` look as wide as for `down`?\n")
```

```{r}
# R/08_fit_stan_lag1.R
# Fit the single-item hierarchical lag-1 VAR (DTVEM-RE simplified)
# on Fisher's `down` data.

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(cmdstanr)
library(posterior)
library(bayesplot)

# === Load and prep data ===
fisher_all <- readRDS(here("data", "processed", "fisher_all.rds"))

if (!"session" %in% colnames(fisher_all)) {
  fisher_all <- fisher_all %>%
    group_by(ID) %>%
    arrange(start_time) %>%
    mutate(session = cumsum(replace_na(gap_hrs > 72, FALSE)) + 1) %>%
    ungroup()
}

target_item <- "down"

# Build lag-1 dataset
prep <- fisher_all %>%
  filter(session == 1) %>%
  drop_na(all_of(target_item)) %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  arrange(start_time) %>%
  mutate(
    y_z = as.numeric(scale(.data[[target_item]])),
    y_lag1 = lag(y_z, 1)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  drop_na(y_z, y_lag1) %>%
  mutate(person = as.integer(as.factor(ID)))

cat("Total observations after lag construction:", nrow(prep), "\n")
cat("Number of people:", n_distinct(prep$person), "\n")

# === Build Stan data list ===
stan_data <- list(
  N = nrow(prep),
  P = n_distinct(prep$person),
  person = prep$person,
  y = prep$y_z,
  y_lag1 = prep$y_lag1
)

# === Compile the model ===
cat("\nCompiling Stan model... (~30 sec on first run)\n")
mod <- cmdstan_model(here("stan", "dtvem_re_lag1.stan"))

# === Fit ===
cat("\nFitting... (~2-5 minutes)\n")
fit <- mod$sample(
  data = stan_data,
  chains = 4,
  parallel_chains = 4,
  iter_warmup = 1000,
  iter_sampling = 1000,
  seed = 42,
  refresh = 200
)

# === Diagnostics ===
cat("\n=== Convergence diagnostics ===\n")
print(fit$diagnostic_summary())

cat("\n=== Population-level parameters ===\n")
print(fit$summary(variables = c("mu_a", "tau_a", "sigma_mean", "sigma_sd",
                                "prop_var_explained_by_persons")))

# === Person-specific posterior summary ===
person_summary <- fit$summary(variables = "a") %>%
  mutate(person = as.integer(str_extract(variable, "\\d+"))) %>%
  arrange(person)

cat("\n=== First 10 person-specific lag-1 coefficients ===\n")
print(person_summary %>% select(person, mean, sd, q5, q95) %>% head(10))

# === Compare to pilot GAMM estimates ===
pilot <- readRDS(here("output", "person_smooths", "per_person_results.rds"))
gamm_lag1 <- pilot$down$person_lag1 %>%
  mutate(ID = as.character(ID)) %>%
  arrange(ID)

person_summary <- person_summary %>%
  mutate(ID = levels(as.factor(prep$ID))[person]) %>%
  left_join(gamm_lag1, by = "ID")

# Correlation between Stan posterior means and GAMM estimates
r <- cor(person_summary$mean, person_summary$lag1_effect)
cat("\n=== Correlation between Stan posterior mean and GAMM estimate ===\n")
cat("r =", round(r, 3), "\n")
cat("(Hypothesis 2b said this should be > 0.85)\n")

# === Save fit and plots ===
dir.create(here("output", "stan_fits"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
fit$save_object(here("output", "stan_fits", "lag1_down.rds"))

# Plot 1: posterior of mu_a and tau_a
post_draws <- fit$draws(variables = c("mu_a", "tau_a"), format = "df")

p1 <- mcmc_dens(fit$draws(c("mu_a", "tau_a")))
ggsave(here("output", "stan_fits", "01_mu_tau_posteriors.png"),
       p1, width = 10, height = 4, dpi = 150)

# Plot 2: Stan vs GAMM person-specific estimates
p2 <- ggplot(person_summary, aes(x = lag1_effect, y = mean)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = q5, ymax = q95), color = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Stan vs GAMM person-specific lag-1 estimates (", target_item, ")"),
    subtitle = paste0("r = ", round(r, 3),
                      "; Dashed line = perfect agreement"),
    x = "GAMM estimate (pilot)",
    y = "Stan posterior mean (with 90% CI)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

print(p2)
ggsave(here("output", "stan_fits", "02_stan_vs_gamm.png"),
       p2, width = 8, height = 8, dpi = 150)

# Plot 3: caterpillar plot of all person-specific coefficients
p3 <- person_summary %>%
  arrange(mean) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number()) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = rank, y = mean)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(person_summary$mean), 
             color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = q5, ymax = q95), color = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Person-specific lag-1 coefficients (sorted)",
    subtitle = "Red line = population mean μ_a; Bars = 90% credible intervals",
    x = "Person (sorted by posterior mean)",
    y = "Lag-1 AR coefficient"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

print(p3)
ggsave(here("output", "stan_fits", "03_person_caterpillar.png"),
       p3, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 150)

cat("\nDone. Plots saved to output/stan_fits/.\n")
```

```{r}
# R/11_refit_all_v2.R
# Refit all three items with the v2 (non-centered sigma) model for consistency

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(cmdstanr)

fisher_all <- readRDS(here("data", "processed", "fisher_all.rds"))

if (!"session" %in% colnames(fisher_all)) {
  fisher_all <- fisher_all %>%
    group_by(ID) %>%
    arrange(start_time) %>%
    mutate(session = cumsum(replace_na(gap_hrs > 72, FALSE)) + 1) %>%
    ungroup()
}

mod_v2 <- cmdstan_model(here("stan", "dtvem_re_lag1_v2.stan"))

fit_one <- function(item) {
  cat("\n=== Fitting v2 for:", item, "===\n")
  
  prep <- fisher_all %>%
    filter(session == 1) %>%
    drop_na(all_of(item)) %>%
    group_by(ID) %>%
    arrange(start_time) %>%
    mutate(y_z = as.numeric(scale(.data[[item]])), y_lag1 = lag(y_z, 1)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    drop_na(y_z, y_lag1) %>%
    mutate(person = as.integer(as.factor(ID)))
  
  stan_data <- list(
    N = nrow(prep),
    P = n_distinct(prep$person),
    person = prep$person,
    y = prep$y_z,
    y_lag1 = prep$y_lag1
  )
  
  fit <- mod_v2$sample(
    data = stan_data,
    chains = 4, parallel_chains = 4,
    iter_warmup = 1000, iter_sampling = 1000,
    seed = 42, refresh = 0, adapt_delta = 0.95
  )
  
  diag <- fit$diagnostic_summary()
  cat("Divergences:", sum(diag$num_divergent), 
      "| Min EBFMI:", round(min(diag$ebfmi), 3), "\n")
  
  fit$save_object(here("output", "stan_fits", paste0("lag1_", item, "_v2.rds")))
  
  fit$summary(variables = c("mu_a", "tau_a", "sigma_mean", "sigma_sd",
                             "prop_var_explained_by_persons")) %>%
    mutate(item = item)
}

results <- map_dfr(c("down", "worried", "energetic"), fit_one)

cat("\n\n=== FINAL v2 RESULTS (all three items) ===\n")
print(results %>% 
        select(item, variable, mean, sd, q5, q95) %>% 
        mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 3))))

write_csv(results, here("output", "stan_fits", "v2_all_items_summary.csv"))
```

```{r}
# R/12_simulation_aim1.R
# Aim 1: simulation study validating DTVEM-RE parameter recovery.
# Design: 4 heterogeneity levels (tau_a = 0, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30)
#         × 30 replicates each = 120 total fits.

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(cmdstanr)
library(posterior)

# === Settings ===
N_PERSONS <- 40
T_OBS <- 130
TRUE_MU <- 0.4
TAU_LEVELS <- c(0, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30)
N_REPS <- 30
SEED_BASE <- 12345
TOTAL_FITS <- length(TAU_LEVELS) * N_REPS

# Set up logging
dir.create(here("output", "simulation"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
log_file <- here("output", "simulation", "sim_log.txt")
cat(sprintf("Simulation started at %s\n", Sys.time()), file = log_file)
cat(sprintf("Total fits planned: %d\n\n", TOTAL_FITS), file = log_file, append = TRUE)

# === Generate one dataset ===
simulate_data <- function(mu_a, tau_a, sigma_mean = 0.9, 
                          N = N_PERSONS, T = T_OBS, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  
  a_true <- rnorm(N, mu_a, tau_a)
  a_true <- pmax(pmin(a_true, 0.95), -0.95)
  sigma_true <- rlnorm(N, log(sigma_mean), 0.1)
  
  rows <- list()
  for (i in 1:N) {
    y <- numeric(T)
    y[1] <- rnorm(1, 0, sigma_true[i] / sqrt(1 - a_true[i]^2))
    for (t in 2:T) {
      y[t] <- a_true[i] * y[t-1] + rnorm(1, 0, sigma_true[i])
    }
    y_z <- y - mean(y)   # demean but don't scale
    rows[[i]] <- tibble(
      person = i,
      t = 1:T,
      y_z = y_z,
      y_lag1 = lag(y_z, 1)
    )
  }
  
  df <- bind_rows(rows) %>% drop_na(y_lag1)
  
  list(
    df = df,
    a_true = a_true,
    sigma_true = sigma_true,
    mu_a_true = mu_a,
    tau_a_true = tau_a
  )
}

# === Compile model once ===
cat("Compiling v2 Stan model...\n")
mod <- cmdstan_model(here("stan", "dtvem_re_lag1_v2.stan"))
cat("Compilation done.\n\n")

# === Run one replicate ===
run_one_replicate <- function(tau_true, rep_id) {
  seed <- SEED_BASE + tau_true * 1000 + rep_id
  
  sim <- simulate_data(mu_a = TRUE_MU, tau_a = tau_true, seed = seed)
  
  stan_data <- list(
    N = nrow(sim$df),
    P = N_PERSONS,
    person = sim$df$person,
    y = sim$df$y_z,
    y_lag1 = sim$df$y_lag1
  )
  
  fit <- mod$sample(
    data = stan_data,
    chains = 2, parallel_chains = 2,
    iter_warmup = 500, iter_sampling = 500,
    seed = seed, refresh = 0, adapt_delta = 0.95,
    show_messages = FALSE, show_exceptions = FALSE
  )
  
  diag <- fit$diagnostic_summary(quiet = TRUE)
  
  pop_summary <- fit$summary(variables = c("mu_a", "tau_a"))
  mu_row <- pop_summary[pop_summary$variable == "mu_a", ]
  tau_row <- pop_summary[pop_summary$variable == "tau_a", ]
  
  tibble(
    tau_true = tau_true,
    rep_id = rep_id,
    mu_true = TRUE_MU,
    mu_est = mu_row$mean,
    mu_q5 = mu_row$q5,
    mu_q95 = mu_row$q95,
    mu_covered = mu_row$q5 <= TRUE_MU & TRUE_MU <= mu_row$q95,
    tau_est = tau_row$mean,
    tau_q5 = tau_row$q5,
    tau_q95 = tau_row$q95,
    tau_covered = tau_row$q5 <= tau_true & tau_true <= tau_row$q95,
    n_divergent = sum(diag$num_divergent),
    min_ebfmi = min(diag$ebfmi)
  )
}

# === Main loop ===
results <- list()
start_time <- Sys.time()
fit_counter <- 0

for (tau_level in TAU_LEVELS) {
  for (rep in 1:N_REPS) {
    fit_counter <- fit_counter + 1
    
    # Progress with ETA
    elapsed_min <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start_time, units = "mins"))
    if (fit_counter > 1) {
      avg_min_per_fit <- elapsed_min / (fit_counter - 1)
      remaining_min <- avg_min_per_fit * (TOTAL_FITS - fit_counter + 1)
      eta_str <- sprintf(" | ETA: %.1f min remaining", remaining_min)
    } else {
      eta_str <- ""
    }
    
    msg <- sprintf("[%s] Fit %d/%d: tau_true=%.2f rep=%d%s\n",
                   format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"), 
                   fit_counter, TOTAL_FITS, 
                   tau_level, rep, eta_str)
    cat(msg)
    cat(msg, file = log_file, append = TRUE)
    
    res <- tryCatch(
      run_one_replicate(tau_level, rep),
      error = function(e) {
        err_msg <- sprintf("  ERROR: %s\n", conditionMessage(e))
        cat(err_msg)
        cat(err_msg, file = log_file, append = TRUE)
        NULL
      }
    )
    
    if (!is.null(res)) results[[length(results) + 1]] <- res
    
    # Save partial results every 10 fits
    if (fit_counter %% 10 == 0) {
      saveRDS(bind_rows(results), 
              here("output", "simulation", "sim_results_partial.rds"))
      cat(sprintf("  (Saved %d partial results)\n", length(results)))
    }
  }
}

total_min <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start_time, units = "mins"))
final_msg <- sprintf("\nDone! Total time: %.1f minutes. Successful fits: %d/%d\n",
                     total_min, length(results), TOTAL_FITS)
cat(final_msg)
cat(final_msg, file = log_file, append = TRUE)

sim_results <- bind_rows(results)
saveRDS(sim_results, here("output", "simulation", "sim_results.rds"))

# === Summary ===
summary_table <- sim_results %>%
  group_by(tau_true) %>%
  summarise(
    n_reps = n(),
    mu_mean_est = mean(mu_est),
    mu_bias = mean(mu_est) - TRUE_MU,
    mu_rmse = sqrt(mean((mu_est - TRUE_MU)^2)),
    mu_coverage = mean(mu_covered),
    tau_mean_est = mean(tau_est),
    tau_bias = mean(tau_est - tau_true),
    tau_rmse = sqrt(mean((tau_est - tau_true)^2)),
    tau_coverage = mean(tau_covered),
    pct_clean_diagnostics = mean(n_divergent == 0 & min_ebfmi > 0.3),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("\n=== SIMULATION SUMMARY ===\n")
print(summary_table %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 3))))

write_csv(summary_table, here("output", "simulation", "sim_summary.csv"))

# === Plots ===

# 1. Tau recovery plot
p_tau <- sim_results %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(tau_true), y = tau_est)) +
  geom_hline(data = tibble(tau_true = TAU_LEVELS), 
             aes(yintercept = tau_true), 
             color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "DTVEM-RE recovery of between-person SD (τ_a)",
    subtitle = "Red dashes = true values; Each point = one simulation replicate",
    x = "True τ_a",
    y = "Estimated τ_a (posterior mean)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

print(p_tau)
ggsave(here("output", "simulation", "tau_recovery.png"),
       p_tau, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 150)

# 2. Mu recovery plot
p_mu <- sim_results %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(tau_true), y = mu_est)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = TRUE_MU, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "DTVEM-RE recovery of population mean (μ_a)",
    subtitle = sprintf("Red dashes = true μ_a = %.2f; Each point = one replicate", TRUE_MU),
    x = "True τ_a",
    y = "Estimated μ_a (posterior mean)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

print(p_mu)
ggsave(here("output", "simulation", "mu_recovery.png"),
       p_mu, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 150)

# 3. Coverage plot
p_coverage <- summary_table %>%
  select(tau_true, mu_coverage, tau_coverage) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(mu_coverage, tau_coverage), 
               names_to = "param", values_to = "coverage") %>%
  mutate(param = if_else(param == "mu_coverage", "μ_a", "τ_a")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(tau_true), y = coverage, fill = param)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.90, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  ylim(0, 1) +
  labs(
    title = "90% credible interval coverage",
    subtitle = "Red dashed = nominal 90% coverage",
    x = "True τ_a",
    y = "Empirical coverage",
    fill = "Parameter"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("μ_a" = "steelblue", "τ_a" = "coral"))

print(p_coverage)
ggsave(here("output", "simulation", "coverage.png"),
       p_coverage, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 150)

cat("\nAll done. See output/simulation/ for results and plots.\n")
```

```{r}
# R/13_held_out_prediction.R
# Held-out prediction comparison across four lag-1 methods.
# Holds out last 3 days (~12 beeps) per person; fits on the rest.
# Compares predictive log-likelihood.

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(cmdstanr)
library(posterior)

# ===== Load data =====
fisher_all <- readRDS(here("data", "processed", "fisher_all.rds"))

if (!"session" %in% colnames(fisher_all)) {
  fisher_all <- fisher_all %>%
    group_by(ID) %>%
    arrange(start_time) %>%
    mutate(session = cumsum(replace_na(gap_hrs > 72, FALSE)) + 1) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# Settings
target_item <- "down"  # Run on `down` first; replicate on others later
N_HOLDOUT_BEEPS <- 12  # Approximately last 3 days at 4 beeps/day

# ===== Prepare train/test split =====

prep_split <- fisher_all %>%
  filter(session == 1) %>%
  drop_na(all_of(target_item)) %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  arrange(start_time) %>%
  mutate(
    y_z = as.numeric(scale(.data[[target_item]])),
    y_lag1 = lag(y_z, 1),
    beep_num = row_number(),
    total_beeps = n()
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  drop_na(y_z, y_lag1) %>%
  # Mark last N_HOLDOUT_BEEPS per person as test
  group_by(ID) %>%
  mutate(
    is_test = beep_num > (max(beep_num) - N_HOLDOUT_BEEPS)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(person = as.integer(as.factor(ID)))

train <- prep_split %>% filter(!is_test)
test <- prep_split %>% filter(is_test)

cat("Train obs:", nrow(train), " | Test obs:", nrow(test), "\n")
cat("Persons:", n_distinct(prep_split$person), "\n")
cat("Avg test beeps per person:", round(nrow(test)/n_distinct(prep_split$person), 1), "\n")

# Output directory
dir.create(here("output", "prediction"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# ===== Method 1: Group-only DTVEM (single a, single sigma) =====
cat("\n--- Method 1: Group-only DTVEM ---\n")

# Simple OLS on pooled data
fit_group <- lm(y_z ~ y_lag1 - 1, data = train)
a_group <- coef(fit_group)["y_lag1"]
sigma_group <- summary(fit_group)$sigma

cat("a_group:", round(a_group, 3), " | sigma_group:", round(sigma_group, 3), "\n")

# Predict held-out
test$pred_group <- a_group * test$y_lag1
test$loglik_group <- dnorm(test$y_z, mean = test$pred_group, 
                            sd = sigma_group, log = TRUE)

# ===== Method 2: Naive per-person DTVEM =====
cat("\n--- Method 2: Naive per-person DTVEM ---\n")

per_person_fits <- train %>%
  group_by(ID, person) %>%
  summarise(
    n_train = n(),
    a_naive = coef(lm(y_z ~ y_lag1 - 1))[1],
    sigma_naive = summary(lm(y_z ~ y_lag1 - 1))$sigma,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Some persons may have very few train obs and unstable estimates; clip to range
per_person_fits <- per_person_fits %>%
  mutate(
    a_naive = pmax(pmin(a_naive, 0.99), -0.99),
    sigma_naive = pmax(sigma_naive, 0.1)
  )

cat("Per-person a range:", round(range(per_person_fits$a_naive), 3), "\n")

# Predict held-out
test <- test %>%
  left_join(per_person_fits %>% select(person, a_naive, sigma_naive), by = "person") %>%
  mutate(
    pred_naive = a_naive * y_lag1,
    loglik_naive = dnorm(y_z, mean = pred_naive, sd = sigma_naive, log = TRUE)
  )

# ===== Method 3: Hierarchical lag-1 in Stan (= our DTVEM-RE without sigma hierarchy) =====
cat("\n--- Method 3: Hierarchical lag-1 (mlVAR-style baseline) ---\n")

# Build a simpler Stan model with hierarchical a but single sigma
simple_stan_code <- "
data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=1> P;
  array[N] int<lower=1,upper=P> person;
  vector[N] y;
  vector[N] y_lag1;
}
parameters {
  real mu_a;
  real<lower=0> tau_a;
  vector[P] a_raw;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[P] a = mu_a + tau_a * a_raw;
}
model {
  mu_a ~ normal(0, 0.5);
  tau_a ~ normal(0, 0.3);
  a_raw ~ std_normal();
  sigma ~ normal(0.9, 0.3);
  for (n in 1:N) {
    y[n] ~ normal(a[person[n]] * y_lag1[n], sigma);
  }
}
"

# Write to temp file
simple_stan_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".stan")
writeLines(simple_stan_code, simple_stan_file)

mod_simple <- cmdstan_model(simple_stan_file)

stan_data_simple <- list(
  N = nrow(train),
  P = n_distinct(train$person),
  person = train$person,
  y = train$y_z,
  y_lag1 = train$y_lag1
)

fit_simple <- mod_simple$sample(
  data = stan_data_simple,
  chains = 4, parallel_chains = 4,
  iter_warmup = 1000, iter_sampling = 1000,
  seed = 123, refresh = 0
)

a_simple <- fit_simple$summary("a")$mean
sigma_simple <- fit_simple$summary("sigma")$mean

test <- test %>%
  mutate(
    a_simple = a_simple[person],
    pred_simple = a_simple * y_lag1,
    loglik_simple = dnorm(y_z, mean = pred_simple, sd = sigma_simple, log = TRUE)
  )

# ===== Method 4: Full DTVEM-RE (v2 model with hierarchical sigma) =====
cat("\n--- Method 4: Full DTVEM-RE ---\n")

mod_full <- cmdstan_model(here("stan", "dtvem_re_lag1_v2.stan"))

stan_data_full <- list(
  N = nrow(train),
  P = n_distinct(train$person),
  person = train$person,
  y = train$y_z,
  y_lag1 = train$y_lag1
)

fit_full <- mod_full$sample(
  data = stan_data_full,
  chains = 4, parallel_chains = 4,
  iter_warmup = 1000, iter_sampling = 1000,
  seed = 123, refresh = 0, adapt_delta = 0.95
)

a_full <- fit_full$summary("a")$mean
sigma_full <- fit_full$summary("sigma")$mean

test <- test %>%
  mutate(
    a_full = a_full[person],
    sigma_full = sigma_full[person],
    pred_full = a_full * y_lag1,
    loglik_full = dnorm(y_z, mean = pred_full, sd = sigma_full, log = TRUE)
  )

# ===== Compare methods =====
cat("\n\n==== HELD-OUT PREDICTION RESULTS ====\n")

method_summary <- tibble(
  method = c("1. Group-only DTVEM", "2. Naive per-person", 
             "3. Hierarchical (mlVAR)", "4. DTVEM-RE (full)"),
  mean_loglik = c(mean(test$loglik_group),
                   mean(test$loglik_naive),
                   mean(test$loglik_simple),
                   mean(test$loglik_full)),
  total_loglik = c(sum(test$loglik_group),
                    sum(test$loglik_naive),
                    sum(test$loglik_simple),
                    sum(test$loglik_full)),
  rmse = c(sqrt(mean((test$y_z - test$pred_group)^2)),
            sqrt(mean((test$y_z - test$pred_naive)^2)),
            sqrt(mean((test$y_z - test$pred_simple)^2)),
            sqrt(mean((test$y_z - test$pred_full)^2)))
)

print(method_summary %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 4))))

write_csv(method_summary, here("output", "prediction", 
                                paste0("comparison_", target_item, ".csv")))

# ===== Per-person comparison: where does DTVEM-RE help most? =====
per_person_loglik <- test %>%
  group_by(person, ID) %>%
  summarise(
    n_test = n(),
    ll_group = mean(loglik_group),
    ll_naive = mean(loglik_naive),
    ll_simple = mean(loglik_simple),
    ll_full = mean(loglik_full),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(per_person_fits %>% select(person, n_train), by = "person") %>%
  mutate(
    full_vs_group = ll_full - ll_group,
    full_vs_naive = ll_full - ll_naive,
    full_vs_simple = ll_full - ll_simple
  )

cat("\n=== Per-person DTVEM-RE advantage ===\n")
cat("DTVEM-RE vs Group-only: mean ", round(mean(per_person_loglik$full_vs_group), 4),
    "| % better: ", round(mean(per_person_loglik$full_vs_group > 0) * 100, 1), "%\n")
cat("DTVEM-RE vs Naive:      mean ", round(mean(per_person_loglik$full_vs_naive), 4),
    "| % better: ", round(mean(per_person_loglik$full_vs_naive > 0) * 100, 1), "%\n")
cat("DTVEM-RE vs Hier-simple: mean ", round(mean(per_person_loglik$full_vs_simple), 4),
    "| % better: ", round(mean(per_person_loglik$full_vs_simple > 0) * 100, 1), "%\n")

# ===== Plots =====

# Plot 1: methods compared
p1 <- method_summary %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(method, mean_loglik), y = mean_loglik)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(mean_loglik, 4)), 
            vjust = -0.5, size = 4) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Held-out predictive log-likelihood (", target_item, ")"),
    subtitle = paste0("Higher is better. ", nrow(test), " held-out beeps across 40 people."),
    x = "Method",
    y = "Mean log-likelihood per held-out beep"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))

print(p1)
ggsave(here("output", "prediction", paste0("methods_comparison_", target_item, ".png")),
       p1, width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 150)

# Plot 2: per-person DTVEM-RE advantage over naive
p2 <- per_person_loglik %>%
  arrange(full_vs_naive) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number()) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = rank, y = full_vs_naive)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_col(aes(fill = full_vs_naive > 0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "coral", "TRUE" = "steelblue"),
                    name = "DTVEM-RE wins?") +
  labs(
    title = "Per-person prediction: DTVEM-RE vs Naive per-person",
    subtitle = "Positive bars = DTVEM-RE predicts better; ranked by advantage",
    x = "Person (ranked)",
    y = "Log-likelihood improvement"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

print(p2)
ggsave(here("output", "prediction", paste0("per_person_advantage_", target_item, ".png")),
       p2, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 150)

saveRDS(per_person_loglik, here("output", "prediction", 
                                  paste0("per_person_results_", target_item, ".rds")))

cat("\nDone. Outputs in output/prediction/.\n")
```

```{r}
# R/14_small_n_prediction.R
# Test whether DTVEM-RE's predictive advantage grows at smaller per-person T.
# Same setup as R/13_held_out_prediction.R but with three training-data sizes.

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(cmdstanr)

# ===== Settings =====
target_item <- "down"
T_TRAIN_LEVELS <- c(30, 50, 100)
N_HOLDOUT_BEEPS <- 12

# ===== Load data =====
fisher_all <- readRDS(here("data", "processed", "fisher_all.rds"))

if (!"session" %in% colnames(fisher_all)) {
  fisher_all <- fisher_all %>%
    group_by(ID) %>%
    arrange(start_time) %>%
    mutate(session = cumsum(replace_na(gap_hrs > 72, FALSE)) + 1) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# ===== Prepare data =====
prep_full <- fisher_all %>%
  filter(session == 1) %>%
  drop_na(all_of(target_item)) %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  arrange(start_time) %>%
  mutate(
    y_z = as.numeric(scale(.data[[target_item]])),
    y_lag1 = lag(y_z, 1),
    beep_num = row_number(),
    total_beeps = n()
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  drop_na(y_z, y_lag1) %>%
  mutate(person = as.integer(as.factor(ID)))

# Compile Stan models
mod_full <- cmdstan_model(here("stan", "dtvem_re_lag1_v2.stan"))

# Simple hierarchical model (shared sigma)
simple_stan_code <- "
data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=1> P;
  array[N] int<lower=1,upper=P> person;
  vector[N] y;
  vector[N] y_lag1;
}
parameters {
  real mu_a;
  real<lower=0> tau_a;
  vector[P] a_raw;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[P] a = mu_a + tau_a * a_raw;
}
model {
  mu_a ~ normal(0, 0.5);
  tau_a ~ normal(0, 0.3);
  a_raw ~ std_normal();
  sigma ~ normal(0.9, 0.3);
  for (n in 1:N) {
    y[n] ~ normal(a[person[n]] * y_lag1[n], sigma);
  }
}
"
simple_stan_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".stan")
writeLines(simple_stan_code, simple_stan_file)
mod_simple <- cmdstan_model(simple_stan_file)

# ===== Function to run all 4 methods at one T_train level =====
run_comparison <- function(T_train) {
  cat(sprintf("\n\n========== T_train = %d ==========\n", T_train))
  
  # Create train/test split with limited T_train
  prep_split <- prep_full %>%
    group_by(person) %>%
    arrange(beep_num) %>%
    mutate(
      # Determine the cutoff: use first T_train beeps for train,
      # then skip ahead and use the last N_HOLDOUT_BEEPS as test.
      # Held-out beeps are always the most recent N_HOLDOUT_BEEPS.
      max_beep = max(beep_num),
      is_train = beep_num <= T_train,
      is_test = beep_num > (max_beep - N_HOLDOUT_BEEPS)
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  train <- prep_split %>% filter(is_train)
  test <- prep_split %>% filter(is_test)
  
  cat(sprintf("Train: %d obs (~%d per person)\n", nrow(train), 
              round(nrow(train) / n_distinct(train$person))))
  cat(sprintf("Test: %d obs (~%d per person)\n", nrow(test),
              round(nrow(test) / n_distinct(test$person))))
  
  # --- Method 1: Group-only OLS ---
  fit_group <- lm(y_z ~ y_lag1 - 1, data = train)
  a_group <- coef(fit_group)["y_lag1"]
  sigma_group <- summary(fit_group)$sigma
  
  test$pred_group <- a_group * test$y_lag1
  test$loglik_group <- dnorm(test$y_z, test$pred_group, sigma_group, log = TRUE)
  
  # --- Method 2: Naive per-person OLS ---
  per_person_fits <- train %>%
    group_by(person) %>%
    summarise(
      n_train = n(),
      a_naive = ifelse(n_train >= 3,
                       coef(lm(y_z ~ y_lag1 - 1))[1], 0),
      sigma_naive = ifelse(n_train >= 3,
                           summary(lm(y_z ~ y_lag1 - 1))$sigma, 1),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      a_naive = pmax(pmin(a_naive, 0.99), -0.99),
      sigma_naive = pmax(sigma_naive, 0.1)
    )
  
  test <- test %>%
    left_join(per_person_fits %>% select(person, a_naive, sigma_naive), 
              by = "person") %>%
    mutate(
      pred_naive = a_naive * y_lag1,
      loglik_naive = dnorm(y_z, pred_naive, sigma_naive, log = TRUE)
    )
  
  # --- Method 3: Hierarchical simple (mlVAR-style) ---
  stan_data <- list(
    N = nrow(train), P = n_distinct(train$person),
    person = train$person, y = train$y_z, y_lag1 = train$y_lag1
  )
  
  fit_simple <- mod_simple$sample(
    data = stan_data, chains = 4, parallel_chains = 4,
    iter_warmup = 1000, iter_sampling = 1000,
    seed = 123, refresh = 0
  )
  
  a_simple <- fit_simple$summary("a")$mean
  sigma_simple <- fit_simple$summary("sigma")$mean
  
  test <- test %>%
    mutate(
      a_simple = a_simple[person],
      pred_simple = a_simple * y_lag1,
      loglik_simple = dnorm(y_z, pred_simple, sigma_simple, log = TRUE)
    )
  
  # --- Method 4: Full DTVEM-RE ---
  fit_full <- mod_full$sample(
    data = stan_data, chains = 4, parallel_chains = 4,
    iter_warmup = 1000, iter_sampling = 1000,
    seed = 123, refresh = 0, adapt_delta = 0.95
  )
  
  a_full <- fit_full$summary("a")$mean
  sigma_full <- fit_full$summary("sigma")$mean
  
  test <- test %>%
    mutate(
      a_full = a_full[person],
      sigma_full = sigma_full[person],
      pred_full = a_full * y_lag1,
      loglik_full = dnorm(y_z, pred_full, sigma_full, log = TRUE)
    )
  
  # Summary table
  summary_row <- tibble(
    T_train = T_train,
    method = c("Group-only", "Naive per-person", "Hierarchical simple", "DTVEM-RE"),
    mean_loglik = c(mean(test$loglik_group),
                     mean(test$loglik_naive),
                     mean(test$loglik_simple),
                     mean(test$loglik_full)),
    rmse = c(sqrt(mean((test$y_z - test$pred_group)^2)),
              sqrt(mean((test$y_z - test$pred_naive)^2)),
              sqrt(mean((test$y_z - test$pred_simple)^2)),
              sqrt(mean((test$y_z - test$pred_full)^2)))
  )
  
  # DTVEM-RE advantage stats
  advantage <- tibble(
    T_train = T_train,
    full_vs_group = mean(test$loglik_full - test$loglik_group),
    full_vs_naive = mean(test$loglik_full - test$loglik_naive),
    full_vs_simple = mean(test$loglik_full - test$loglik_simple),
    pct_full_beats_naive = mean(test$loglik_full > test$loglik_naive) * 100
  )
  
  cat("\nMethod comparison:\n")
  print(summary_row %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 4))))
  
  cat("\nDTVEM-RE advantage:\n")
  print(advantage %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 4))))
  
  list(summary = summary_row, advantage = advantage)
}

# ===== Run for each T_train level =====
all_results <- map(T_TRAIN_LEVELS, run_comparison)

# ===== Aggregate =====
dir.create(here("output", "prediction"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

all_summary <- map_dfr(all_results, "summary")
all_advantage <- map_dfr(all_results, "advantage")

cat("\n\n=========== ACROSS ALL T_TRAIN LEVELS ===========\n")
cat("\nMethod log-likelihoods:\n")
print(all_summary %>% 
        pivot_wider(id_cols = T_train, names_from = method, values_from = mean_loglik) %>%
        mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 4))))

cat("\nDTVEM-RE advantage by T_train:\n")
print(all_advantage %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 4))))

write_csv(all_summary, here("output", "prediction", "small_n_summary.csv"))
write_csv(all_advantage, here("output", "prediction", "small_n_advantage.csv"))

# ===== Visualization =====
p_comparison <- all_summary %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(T_train), y = mean_loglik, fill = method)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(mean_loglik, 3)), 
            position = position_dodge(0.9), vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Held-out prediction by training sample size (", target_item, ")"),
    subtitle = "Higher log-likelihood = better; comparison across methods at varying T_train",
    x = "Training observations per person",
    y = "Mean log-likelihood per held-out beep"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

print(p_comparison)
ggsave(here("output", "prediction", "small_n_comparison.png"),
       p_comparison, width = 11, height = 6, dpi = 150)

p_advantage <- all_advantage %>%
  select(T_train, full_vs_group, full_vs_naive, full_vs_simple) %>%
  pivot_longer(-T_train, names_to = "comparison", values_to = "advantage") %>%
  mutate(comparison = recode(comparison,
                              full_vs_group = "vs Group-only",
                              full_vs_naive = "vs Naive per-person",
                              full_vs_simple = "vs Hierarchical simple")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(T_train), y = advantage, fill = comparison)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  labs(
    title = "DTVEM-RE predictive advantage shrinks as T_train grows",
    subtitle = "Positive = DTVEM-RE wins; hypothesis: pooling matters most when per-person T is small",
    x = "Training observations per person",
    y = "Log-likelihood improvement over comparison method",
    fill = "DTVEM-RE compared to:"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

print(p_advantage)
ggsave(here("output", "prediction", "small_n_advantage.png"),
       p_advantage, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 150)

cat("\nDone. Outputs in output/prediction/.\n")
```

```{r}
# R/15_fit_stan_multilag.R
# Fit the multi-lag DTVEM-RE model on Fisher's three core items.
# Tests whether person-specific variation extends beyond lag-1.

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(cmdstanr)
library(posterior)

# === Settings ===
K_LAGS <- 3      # estimate lag-1, lag-2, lag-3
TARGET_ITEMS <- c("down", "worried", "energetic")

# === Load data ===
fisher_all <- readRDS(here("data", "processed", "fisher_all.rds"))

if (!"session" %in% colnames(fisher_all)) {
  fisher_all <- fisher_all %>%
    group_by(ID) %>%
    arrange(start_time) %>%
    mutate(session = cumsum(replace_na(gap_hrs > 72, FALSE)) + 1) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# === Compile model ===
cat("Compiling multi-lag Stan model...\n")
mod <- cmdstan_model(here("stan", "dtvem_re_multilag.stan"))
cat("Compilation done.\n")

# === Fit function ===
fit_one_item <- function(item) {
  cat(sprintf("\n\n=========== FITTING: %s ===========\n", item))
  
  # Build lag-augmented dataset with K lags
  prep <- fisher_all %>%
    filter(session == 1) %>%
    drop_na(all_of(item)) %>%
    group_by(ID) %>%
    arrange(start_time) %>%
    mutate(
      y_z = as.numeric(scale(.data[[item]]))
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # Add lagged columns
  for (k in 1:K_LAGS) {
    prep <- prep %>%
      group_by(ID) %>%
      arrange(start_time) %>%
      mutate("y_lag{k}" := lag(y_z, k)) %>%
      ungroup()
  }
  
  # Drop rows with any NA in lagged values
  lag_cols <- paste0("y_lag", 1:K_LAGS)
  prep <- prep %>%
    drop_na(y_z, all_of(lag_cols)) %>%
    mutate(person = as.integer(as.factor(ID)))
  
  cat("Observations after lag construction:", nrow(prep), "\n")
  cat("Persons:", n_distinct(prep$person), "\n")
  
  # Build y_lags matrix
  y_lags_matrix <- as.matrix(prep[, lag_cols])
  
  stan_data <- list(
    N = nrow(prep),
    P = n_distinct(prep$person),
    K = K_LAGS,
    person = prep$person,
    y = prep$y_z,
    y_lags = y_lags_matrix
  )
  
  # Fit
  fit <- mod$sample(
    data = stan_data,
    chains = 4, parallel_chains = 4,
    iter_warmup = 1000, iter_sampling = 1000,
    seed = 42, refresh = 200,
    adapt_delta = 0.95
  )
  
  # Diagnostics
  diag <- fit$diagnostic_summary()
  cat("\n--- Diagnostics ---\n")
  cat("Total divergences:", sum(diag$num_divergent), "\n")
  cat("Min E-BFMI:", round(min(diag$ebfmi), 3), "\n")
  
  # Save
  dir.create(here("output", "stan_fits"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  fit$save_object(here("output", "stan_fits", paste0("multilag_", item, ".rds")))
  
  # Summarize population parameters
  pop_summary <- fit$summary(variables = c("mu_a", "tau_a", "sigma_mean", 
                                            "sigma_sd", "prop_var_from_persons"))
  cat("\n--- Population-level parameters ---\n")
  print(pop_summary %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 4))))
  
  list(item = item, fit = fit, pop_summary = pop_summary, n_obs = nrow(prep))
}

# === Run for all three items ===
all_fits <- map(TARGET_ITEMS, fit_one_item)
names(all_fits) <- TARGET_ITEMS

# === Build cross-item summary ===
cat("\n\n=========== CROSS-ITEM MULTI-LAG SUMMARY ===========\n")

build_lag_summary <- function(res) {
  s <- res$pop_summary %>%
    filter(str_detect(variable, "mu_a\\[|tau_a\\[")) %>%
    separate(variable, into = c("param", "lag"), sep = "\\[") %>%
    mutate(
      lag = as.integer(str_remove(lag, "\\]")),
      item = res$item
    ) %>%
    select(item, param, lag, mean, sd, q5, q95)
  s
}

multilag_summary <- map_dfr(all_fits, build_lag_summary)

# Format for display
display_table <- multilag_summary %>%
  mutate(
    param = if_else(param == "mu_a", "μ", "τ"),
    estimate = sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]", mean, q5, q95)
  ) %>%
  select(item, param, lag, estimate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(param, lag), values_from = estimate,
              names_glue = "{param}_lag{lag}")

print(display_table)

write_csv(multilag_summary, here("output", "stan_fits", "multilag_summary.csv"))

# === Key plots ===

# Plot 1: tau_k across lags and items — does heterogeneity drop off at higher lags?
p_tau <- multilag_summary %>%
  filter(param == "tau_a") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = lag, y = mean, color = item)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = q5, ymax = q95), width = 0.15, position = position_dodge(0.3)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(0.3)) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(0.3)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:K_LAGS) +
  labs(
    title = "Between-person SD (τ_k) at each lag",
    subtitle = "If τ_k > 0 for k > 1, person-specific variation extends beyond lag-1",
    x = "Lag",
    y = "τ_k (with 90% CI)",
    color = "Item"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

print(p_tau)
ggsave(here("output", "stan_fits", "multilag_tau_by_lag.png"),
       p_tau, width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 150)

# Plot 2: mu_k across lags — confirms population-level exponential decay
p_mu <- multilag_summary %>%
  filter(param == "mu_a") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = lag, y = mean, color = item)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = q5, ymax = q95), width = 0.15, position = position_dodge(0.3)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(0.3)) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(0.3)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:K_LAGS) +
  labs(
    title = "Population-level lag coefficients (μ_k) at each lag",
    subtitle = "Expect monotonic decay if Fisher's dynamics follow exponential decay",
    x = "Lag",
    y = "μ_k (with 90% CI)",
    color = "Item"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

print(p_mu)
ggsave(here("output", "stan_fits", "multilag_mu_by_lag.png"),
       p_mu, width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 150)

# Plot 3: Person-specific multi-lag profiles (down only, for clarity)
fit_down <- all_fits$down$fit
person_summary <- fit_down$summary(variables = "a") %>%
  filter(str_detect(variable, "a\\[")) %>%
  separate(variable, into = c("a_label", "indices"), sep = "\\[") %>%
  separate(indices, into = c("lag", "person"), sep = ",") %>%
  mutate(
    lag = as.integer(lag),
    person = as.integer(str_remove(person, "\\]"))
  ) %>%
  select(lag, person, mean, q5, q95)

p_persons <- person_summary %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = lag, y = mean, group = person)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.25, color = "steelblue") +
  stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "line",
               color = "red", linewidth = 1.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:K_LAGS) +
  labs(
    title = "Person-specific lag profiles: down (multi-lag fit)",
    subtitle = "Blue = individual; Red = population average",
    x = "Lag",
    y = "Lag coefficient"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

print(p_persons)
ggsave(here("output", "stan_fits", "multilag_person_profiles_down.png"),
       p_persons, width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 150)

cat("\nDone. Outputs in output/stan_fits/.\n")
```
